To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- the model is able to reproduce qualitatively and quantitatively the seasonal cycle of sulfur species at the sites of observations in Antarctica, and - the model is a useful tool to investigate the sulfur cycle in Antarctica.

- DMS and SO2 emissions from the oceans are a major source of sulfur to the atmosphere in the Southern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and high latitudes; - the atmospheric lifetime of DMS is about one day, and the atmospheric lifetime of SO2 is about one month in the Southern Hemisphere high latitudes; and - most of the SO2 and sulfate in Antarctica are produced by the oxidation of DMS in situ.

(a) the sulfur cycle in the Southern Ocean is driven by a seasonal cycle in DMS emissions, with a maximum in austral summer and a minimum in austral winter, and that the sulfur budget is dominated by the oceanic source of DMS; and (b) the sulfur budget is also influenced by long-range atmospheric transport from the northern mid-latitudes, and by a small oceanic source of H2S, but not by the oceanic emission of SO2.
